[MATH: \dfrac{(x-h)^2}{a^2} - \dfrac{(y-k)^2}{b^2} = 1.]

Content:
The equations of the asymptotes of this horizontal hyperbola, as depicted in the diagram below, are

sections.normalized_html: Calculate the asymptotes of the hyperbola [MATH: \dfrac{(x+2)^2}{18} - \dfrac{(y+7)^2}{32} = 1.]
sections.readable_text: Calculate the asymptotes of the hyperbola [MATH: \dfrac{(x+2)^2}{18} - \dfrac{(y+7)^2}{32} = 1.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
The standard equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at [MATH: (h,k)] is [MATH: \frac{(x-h)^2}{a^2} - \frac{(y-k)^2}{b^2}=1.]

For a horizontal hyperbola, the equations of the asymptotes are

[MATH: y-k=\pm \dfrac{b}{a}(x-h).]

In our case, we have

[MATH: (h,k) = (-2,-7),\qquad a=\sqrt{18} = 3\sqrt{2}, \qquad b=\sqrt{32} = 4\sqrt{2}.]

Therefore, the asymptotes are given by

[MATH: y + 7|= ± ((4sqrt(2))/(3sqrt(2)))(x + 2); y + 7|= ± (4)/(3)(x + 2).]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to group the [MATH: x] and [MATH: y] terms and complete the squares, as follows: [MATH: 9x^{2} − y^{2} − 36x − 2y + 26|= 0; 9x^{2} − 36x − y^{2} − 2y + 26|= 0; 9[x^{2} − 4x] − [y^{2} + 2y] + 26|= 0; 9[(x − 2)^{2} − 4] − [(y + 1)^{2} − 1] + 26|= 0; 9(x − 2)^{2} − 36 − (y + 1)^{2} + 1 + 26|= 0; 9(x − 2)^{2} − (y + 1)^{2}|= − 26 − 1 + 36; 9(x − 2)^{2} − (y + 1)^{2}|= 9; (x − 2)^{2} − ((y + 1)^{2})/(9) = 1]

The asymptotes of the horizontal hyperbola

[MATH: \dfrac{(x-h)^2}{a^2} - \dfrac{(y-k)^2}{b^2} = 1]

are given by [MATH: y-k = \pm\dfrac{b}{a}(x-h).]

In our case, we have [MATH: h = 2, \qquad k = -1, \qquad a = \sqrt{1} = 1,\qquad b = \sqrt{9} = 3.]

Therefore, the asymptotes of the hyperbola are [MATH: y + 1|= ± 3(x − 2).]
